title: Chapter 3 - Probability Distributions

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quick recap on Bayesian Probability:

$$
P(H|D) = \frac{P(D|H)\cdot P(H)}{P(D)}
$$

- $P(H)$: This is the **Prior probability**. It represents the probability of a particular belief or
  hypothesis of being true *before* we have any new data to contrast this belief.
- $P(D|H)$: Frequently called **Likelihood**. From the conditional probablity, this is the
  probability of data being observed if our hypothesis were true. Intuitively, if we collect some
  data that contradicts our beliefs, this probability should be low.
- $P(D)$: It is the measure of all possible ways we could have obtained the data we have. Generally
  considered a normalizing constant.
- $P(H|D)$: This is the **Posterior probability**. From the conditional probability, this represents
  the probability of our hypothesis being true, given that we collected some data *D*.

```{julia}
begin
  using Distributions
  using StatsPlots

  bar(Poisson(1.5), xlabel = "Spam emails", ylabel = "Probability", legend = false,
      size = (400, 300))
end
```
